title: Designing a URL Redirection & Vanity URL Service
subtitle: Start with 200 redirect objects. Earn every component after that.
summary: An evolution-first design of a URL redirection and vanity URL service on AWS: from zero-byte S3 redirect objects to an edge KeyValueStore, a regional Bloom-filter miss guard over DynamoDB, async click attribution and a multi-tenant, multi-Region rule engine. Each level has a trigger, deferred work, build-vs-buy and a sourced cost tier.

quickRead.tldr: Six levels, each earned by a concrete trigger: S3 redirect objects behind CloudFront, a Fargate service over DynamoDB, CloudFront Functions + KeyValueStore at the edge, a Bloom filter in the regional service once 10M+ slugs and bot scans arrive, async click attribution, then a multi-tenant rule engine across three Regions.
keyTakeaways: CloudFront has no declarative redirect rules; start with zero-byte S3 redirect objects (always 301) or Amplify / Cloudflare rules, not a service.
CloudFront KeyValueStore caps at 5 MB per store and 1 KB per value: roughly 50k typical rules (estimate), plenty for a hot set, nowhere near 10M slugs.
A 10M-slug Bloom filter at a 1% false-positive rate is ≈12 MB, too big for KVS or CloudFront Functions, so it guards DynamoDB from inside the regional service while the edge caches 404s.
CloudFront request fees are 55–61% of the bill from L2 up; Firehose's 5 KB per-record rounding is the trap in click tracking.
Global tables are last-writer-wins by default: give each tenant one write Region. Rule compilers and replay verifiers are cheap now; DNS cutover, SEO sign-off and ownership are not.
